clue.text: Flimsy bit of cloth found in record cabinet

indicators.note: the scrap of cloth is found inside the cabinet, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a file is a cabinet or folder where records are kept
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: A thin scrap of fabric turns up inside a filing cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flimsy is delicate and easily broken, a synonym.

clue.text: Bits need softening if settling in

indicators.note: bits signals the letters are broken into bits and reassembled

explanation.surface: Drill bits must be softened if they are to bed in properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bits' sits at the front looking like a noun, but it is the anagram signal, telling us the three words that follow are broken up and reassembled.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming comfortable in a new place or role is an idiom for getting established.

clue.text: Arranged to be outside to snap judge

indicators.note: the abbreviation for arranged goes around the word for snap

parts.note: arr is the abbreviation for arranged, as on music credits
to bite is to snap at

explanation.surface: Someone was set up to stand outside and photograph a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snap' suggests taking a photo, but here it means to bite at; 'to be outside' puts the arranged abbreviation around it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is a person who settles a dispute, as a referee or judge does.

clue.text: Not moving home to provide impetus

parts.note: in means at home
to animate is to give life and drive to something

explanation.surface: A remark that being home inspires someone to act.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless and still objects are inanimate, without motion or life.

clue.text: French in service with English in force

parts.note: en is the French for in
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: French troops serving alongside English forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests the military, but it is a church service, MASS.
explanation.definitionFit: En masse means all together as a body, as a crowd acting in large numbers.

clue.text: Time to pull out

explanation.surface: A sentence telling someone it is time to extract something.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison term is slang for a period of time served, and to extend or draw something out lengthwise is the verb sense.

clue.text: Sorely tempted, succeeded without church involvement

indicators.note: involvement suggests the remaining letters are tangled together and rearranged
without means the letters for church are removed from the word

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A person, badly tempted, managed to win without the church getting involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes C and E out of SUCCEEDED, leaving SUCEDED; 'involvement' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To seduce is to tempt or lure someone astray, so the past form matches tempted.

clue.text: Annoyed and looking embarrassed about one left

indicators.note: about means the colour of embarrassment goes around the other letters

parts.note: someone embarrassed looks red in the face
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone irritated and red-faced as one person departed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be irritated or vexed is to be riled, a synonym.

clue.text: Stumble on oil accidentally in African city

parts.note: to trip is to stumble

indicators.note: accidentally means the letters of oil fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone slips on spilt oil in a North African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Execution done as he stuck around, ashamed

parts.note: hanging is a form of execution

indicators.note: stuck around suggests the letters are jumbled about into a new order

explanation.surface: An execution was carried out while he lingered, feeling disgraced.
explanation.walkthrough: DONE AS HE is rearranged to give the rest of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowering the face in embarrassment is the idiom for feeling shame.

clue.text: Part of Africa that was originally navigated under British imperial authority

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the following words in turn

explanation.surface: A region of Africa once explored and ruled under the British Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of 'navigated under British imperial authority' spell the answer, and the surface is historically apt: the region was under Anglo-Egyptian rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubia is the ancient region along the Nile in southern Egypt and northern Sudan.

clue.text: The compiler (backward youth with big cat) gets an award

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, giving the pronoun me

indicators.note: backward tells us the word for a youth is written in reverse

parts.note: a lad is a youth
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: The setter, together with a shy young man and a lion, is honoured with a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like a description of a shy youth, but it is the reversal signal applied only to the youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a large medal, often given as an honour or prize.

clue.text: Ricin isn't toxic in itself

indicators.note: toxic suggests the letters are poisoned and spoilt, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters I, S, N and T

explanation.surface: A statement that the poison ricin is not inherently harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toxic' fits ricin so well it reads as plain description, but it is the anagram signal for RICIN ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrinsic means belonging to the essential nature of a thing, existing by its own nature.

clue.text: Garment that's popular in the outskirts of Delhi

indicators.note: in places the word for popular inside the other letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters, here of Delhi

parts.note: something hot is popular or in demand

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing that is in fashion on the edges of an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The outskirts of Delhi are its first and last letters, D and I, and HOT goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a loincloth worn by men in India, a type of clothing.

clue.text: Refuse to dress with maturity

parts.note: garb is clothing or dress
age is maturity, having grown old

explanation.surface: Someone declines to put on clothes befitting their years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as the verb to decline, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish thrown away is both refuse and garbage, synonyms.

clue.text: The attraction at home, getting good result?

parts.note: a draw is an attraction, something that pulls in crowds
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A football fan asks whether a crowd-pulling home fixture brings a good outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result' tempts as a match score, but the question mark marks a loose definition: a picture is the result of sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture made with pencil or pen is what an artist produces after sketching, so it is the outcome of that work.

clue.text: A Java programme pictures something to eat

parts.note: an applet is a small application program written in Java
pictures are art

explanation.surface: A coffee-fuelled computer program displays images of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Java' tempts with coffee, but it is the programming language whose small programs are called applets.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit pie is a dessert, so it is food.

clue.text: Puts the weapon back, and obtains valuable little snippets

indicators.note: putting the weapon back means writing its word in reverse

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
gets means obtains

explanation.surface: Someone returns a gun to its place and picks up useful titbits.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuggets are small valuable pieces, like nuggets of information or gold.

clue.text: Deteriorate, having obtained no marijuana

parts.note: got means obtained
O is a nought, meaning no or nothing
pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: A cannabis user goes downhill after failing to score any.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for falling into ruin or decline.

clue.text: Conference remains to be settled

indicators.note: to be settled means the letters are still unsettled and need putting in order

explanation.surface: What is left of the meeting's business still needs agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a meeting for discussion or training.

clue.text: The legend of officer no one backed

parts.note: Capt is the abbreviation for captain, an officer

indicators.note: backed means the words no and one are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tale about a military officer whom nobody supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legend' suggests a story, but it is the words printed under a picture. NO and I reversed give ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is the explanatory text beneath an illustration or map, which is exactly a caption.

clue.text: Jail grim, but with an open quality

parts.note: can is slang for jail
dour means grim and stern

explanation.surface: A bleak prison nevertheless with a frank atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour is openness and honesty in speech, a trait of character.

clue.text: Follow one on the road to the gallery

indicators.note: on means placed on top of, which in a down entry means coming first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Directions telling someone to head down a road toward an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; the Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to copy, following someone's example.

clue.text: The instrument of a positively Spanish sailor

parts.note: si is Spanish for yes, a positive answer
a tar is a sailor, short for tarpaulin

explanation.surface: A musical instrument belonging to an upbeat seaman from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitar is an Indian stringed instrument with a long neck.

clue.text: Country game — adult in each side

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: in places the letter for adult between the side letters

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, each side
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A sports match with a grown-up on both teams.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is rugby union. Right and left are R and L, with A between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural is an adjective for countryside matters, as in country life.

clue.text: Poor specimen includes one of these at Christmas

indicators.note: includes means the letter for one is put inside the rearranged letters
poor suggests a badly made specimen, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A substandard example contains one of the festive treats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges SPECIMEN to MINCEPES, and 'includes' puts I (one) inside to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pastries filled with dried fruit are traditionally eaten in Britain over the festive season.

clue.text: Language repeats on broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A radio station airs reruns of a programme on languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an artificial international tongue invented in the 1880s.

clue.text: Knowing about fights in accident & emergency

indicators.note: in places the word for fights inside the hospital department letters

parts.note: A and E is the hospital casualty department, accident and emergency
war means fighting between sides

explanation.surface: A patient knows about brawls breaking out in a hospital casualty ward.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: To be knowing is to be informed or conscious of something.

clue.text: A turtle turns, providing protection

indicators.note: turns signals that the letters of a turtle are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A turtle rolls over to shield itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' could suggest a reversal, but reading A TURTLE backwards gives nonsense; the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelar describes guardianship, acting as a guardian or protector.

clue.text: Tyre giving outwardly reasonable pace

indicators.note: outwardly takes just the outside letters of reasonable

parts.note: a tread is a step or pace

explanation.surface: A tyre that lets a driver keep up a sensible speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'reasonable' give RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A retread is an old tyre given a new rubber surface.
